concerns.text: SC-005 sets a catastrophic-failure threshold of ≤ 5%, but the evaluation domain is 18 tasks (US-2). One catastrophic failure = 5.6% > 5%, so the criterion is only satisfiable by zero failures. State the criterion in count terms over the 18-task domain (e.g., '≤ 1 of 18 tasks') or define the denominator/repetition count so the threshold is reachable and decidable.

SC-002 and FR-007 require comparison against 'the GPU-based baseline time' / 'GPU-based baseline' compute metrics, but the spec never states where the baseline's CPU-cycle/memory/wall-clock numbers come from. The project runs on CPU-only GitHub Actions runners (Constitution VII, US-1). Name the source of baseline compute measurements (published RoboDojo benchmark numbers, or a documented re-measurement procedure) so the percentage reduction is computable and reproducible.

'System must handle non-unique mappings gracefully or flag for manual review' is not verifiable — 'gracefully' and 'manual review' are undefined behaviors. Specify the observable output (e.g., a logged 'AmbiguousMapping' label with the candidate states, and the task marked as skipped/failed with that label) so the edge case can be confirmed met-or-not.

'attempt to replan from the last known valid state if the policy supports it, or record as a hard failure' leaves the behavior conditional on an unspecified capability. For testability, state which behavior the delivered system MUST exhibit (e.g., always log failure point + label, and record replan-attempt outcome as a logged field), so a test can decide pass/fail deterministically.
